html:
In 1278 the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix signed a paréage, an agreement to share rule over the valleys of Andorra. It created the co-principality that still exists.

The two lords had quarrelled over the valleys for years. They agreed that each would be prince, sharing taxes and justice. The Count of Foix's rights passed to the kings of France and then to the French president, who is still co-prince with the Bishop of Urgell in Spain.

This odd arrangement let the small mountain land stay separate while France and Spain grew around it. The people ran their own affairs through the Council of the Land from 1419. Andorra gained a modern constitution only in 1993. See Andorra and Catalonia.
